plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, often double blooms atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed green foliage. It is a beloved cottage garden staple and can live for decades with little care.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens of North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peony plants can live for over 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not needed for the flowers to open.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen subshrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and spikes of small tubular flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and attracts bees and butterflies in great numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid summer (June to August), beginning in southern regions in late spring
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the western United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash' because the Romans used it to scent baths.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, fast-growing tree with fern-like foliage that is covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it blooms in spring, while in the Northern Hemisphere it peaks in late spring to early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in California, Florida, Mexico, the Mediterranean, and Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas line the streets that the city is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City,' and a carpet of fallen purple blossoms covers the roads.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub that produces the largest flower head in the protea family, with a bowl of pointed pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It is adapted to the nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from roughly May to December and peaks in early winter
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; grown in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The King Protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.
